interventions.who: cohort criterion; what the labelled series did in this exact situation
interventions.body:
This patient's situation: prior positive biopsy. The panel alone does not answer, and that is the finding.

The criterion here is that the visible panel does not determine this decision: he already has a tissue diagnosis, so neither a high PI-RADS nor a rising PSA is new information. What decides it is the documented grade of the prior biopsy and the surveillance history, which live in the previous notes. Measured on the labelled series: none of the three panel
rules I carry for this situation (PSA >= 20, age >= 78, PI-RADS <= 2) applies to him, and among the
39 remaining labelled men in this situation no structured variable separates the two answers.

REGISTRAR: the previous notes are where this case is decided. Read them for the grade of the prior
biopsy (Gleason or ISUP), the number of biopsy sessions and their dates, and whether he is on a
surveillance protocol with a confirmatory biopsy due. Do not read this as 'defer' and do not read it
as 'biopsy'.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The retrieved guidelines discuss using PI-RADS scores and PSA density to guide biopsy decisions. "linking PI-RADS score (1-2, 3, and 4-5) to PSA-D categories (< 0.10, 0.10-0.15, 0.15-0.20 and > 0.20ng/mL) (Table 5.5) [230]. This risk-adapted matrix table may guide the decision to perform a biopsy." This requires establishing the relationship between the PI-RADS score and PSA density for this patient.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
Expert 1's suggestion of biopsy is not settled by the guideline because the guideline requires a risk-adapted matrix based on PI-RADS and PSA density, which is not fully established by the panel variables alone. The cohort criterion notes that none of the panel rules apply, indicating that the decision is not determined by the variables present in the panel.

WHAT WE STILL NEED
The guideline requires establishing the relationship between the PI-RADS score and PSA density for this patient.
The panel already provides: PI-RADS 5 and PSA density of 0.452 ng/mL².
The guideline requires establishing the specific risk-adapted matrix that should be applied to these values to determine the next step.
The prior biopsy status is known as 'Positive', which is a fact already on the panel, but the guideline requires context regarding the documented grade of that prior biopsy to guide the decision.

interventions.speaker: REGISTRAR
interventions.who: the registrar who pulls up documents; reports what they say, nothing else
interventions.body:
WHAT I FOUND
radiology_report
The lesion size and zone is "14 x 12 x 10 mm hypointense focus within the right mid-gland peripheral zone". Extraprostatic extension is "No extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, or suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy is identified". Comparison against an earlier study is "new".
psa_trend
The serial PSA value trend is "rising", with values: "Mar 2023: 4.2", "Nov 2023: 6.2", "Jun 2024: 9.1", "Feb 2025: 13.5".
previous_notes
The prior biopsy grade is "Gleason 3+3, ISUP GG 1". The number and dates of biopsy sessions are "Two systematic biopsies performed in 2023 and 2024". The surveillance protocol status is "under ongoing surveillance".

WHAT I DID NOT OPEN
I did not open the laboratory_results or the family-history anamnesis because the required information regarding the prior biopsy grade and surveillance status was found in the previous_notes.

WHAT THIS SUPPORTS
Findings that argue FOR sampling this patient now:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right mid-gland peripheral zone.
Rising PSA trend from 4.2 ng/mL in Mar 2023 to 13.5 ng/mL in Feb 2025.
csPCa predicted probability of 0.8947026.

Findings that argue AGAINST sampling this patient now:
Prior biopsy grade of "Gleason 3+3, ISUP GG 1".
Patient is currently "under ongoing surveillance".

WHERE THIS LEANS
The documented prior pathology (Gleason 3+3, ISUP GG 1) and the current surveillance status strongly suggest a deferral of immediate biopsy, despite the high PI-RADS score.
LEAN: defer

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 13.50 ng/mL over 4 points spanning 23 months; velocity +4.86 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 14 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 18.6 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 5.3-64.9.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.speaker: VERIFIER
interventions.who: second EAU reader; checks against the guideline whether this can be decided yet
interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents opened by the registrar—radiology_report, psa_trend, and previous_notes—directly address both open questions. The previous_notes explicitly state the prior biopsy grade was "Gleason 3+3, ISUP GG 1" and that the patient is "under ongoing surveillance."

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The PANEL-PROTOCOL concluded BIOPSY based on the EXPERT-LIBRARY precedent, which is supported by the retrieved information. However, the REGISTRAR's finding that the prior grade is "Gleason 3+3, ISUP GG 1" and the surveillance status suggests a conflict with the panel's conclusion.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. What is the documented grade (Gleason or ISUP) of the prior biopsy? Answered by the previous_notes: Gleason 3+3, ISUP GG 1.
Q2. What is the number and dates of previous biopsy sessions, and is the patient on a surveillance protocol with a confirmatory biopsy due? Answered by the previous_notes: Two systematic biopsies performed in 2023 and 2024, and the status is "under ongoing surveillance."

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The documented prior pathology (Gleason 3+3, ISUP GG 1) and the current surveillance status are the most critical variables because they directly inform the risk stratification for re-biopsy, overriding the high PI-RADS score and rising PSA trend.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
I suggest deferral, as the documented prior pathology and current surveillance status strongly argue against immediate biopsy, despite the panel's conclusion.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: defer | MISSING: none
